After editing this file the plugin picks the changes up on the next look — no restart.

capture._note: reuse_seconds avoids taking three screenshots of a screen that has not moved.

_note: Models are tried in the order below, but the client re-orders them by what has
actually been working: a model that has answered quickly before goes first, a model
that returned 404 is remembered as retired and skipped for good, one that returned 503
cools off for 90s, and a model that has never been tried still gets its turn in this
configured order.
Measured on this machine: gemini-3.8-flash returned 503 three times in a row,
gemini-3.7-flash answered once at an average of 15.7s, and gemini-3.5-flash-lite
answered 17 times out of 17 at 2.2s. Without the latency rule the slow-but-alive
model sat at the top and every single look cost 15s.
Enforced in code before an image is sent, not requested in a prompt.
blocked_apps is matched case-insensitively against the app name, window title and
the first few strings of visible text. redact_regions paints rectangles black on the
frame itself, so those pixels never leave the machine.
auto_send false = drafts are written and queued for your approval, never sent.
arm(confirm=true, mode='send') turns unattended sending on for the session.
block_risky_drafts stops anything that promises, agrees to plans, states a time, or
touches money or credentials — those are held for you regardless of mode.
The background loop only runs while armed. It is idempotent: arming twice does
nothing extra. A frame identical to the previous one is skipped without a model call,
which is what keeps a long-running watch cheap.
Copy this block once per person you want Jarvis able to reply to.
Auto-reply is OFF until you set "auto_reply": true for that entry — Jarvis
will draft for anyone it can read, but it will only ever SEND to a contact
whose entry here says auto_reply true.
aliases catch the same person under another spelling. tone/notes are passed to
the drafting prompt as extra guidance for this person only.
